text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Monday:

- U.S. ambassador to Switzerland Madeleine Kunin called for patience with Switzerland with regard to the suspected Jewish funds on Swiss bank accounts. Swiss-American relations were not affected by the this issue, she said in an interview with a U.S. newspaper.
- Private German TV station SAT1 will broadcast Swiss commercials in 1997. It received a relevant permit from Swiss authorities. The commercials will be exclusively broadcasted for Switzerland.

- Swiss Federal Office for Agriculture anounced new legislation that will make the 'bio' food market more transparent. The new laws, which will be introduced in 1997, will make it easier for consumers to trace the origin and the production method of a product.
- Cantonal elections in Basle showed large gains for the Social Democrats.
- Nicolas Hayek, founder and CEO of the lagest Swiss watch and micoelectronic group SMH, received a honorary doctor's degree of the University of Neuenburg.
- Eight people were killed in car accidents on Swiss roads over the weekend.
- Some 100 Christian Social Democratic politicians from several French-speaking cantons and Zurich decided on Sunday to create a national political party.
